text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Italian sculptor and goldsmith BENVENUTO CELLINI was born in 1500.
British Prime Minister SPENCER PERCEVAL (from 1809), who was assassinated in the House Of Commons, was born in 1762.
Irish soldier FRANCIS ALLMAN, who became a pioneer of sugar cane culture in colonial New South Wales at Port Macquarie, was born in 1780.
Colonial pioneer in Western Australia MARSHALL WALLER CLIFTON was born in 1787.
Australian symbolist poet and classical scholar CHRISTOPHER BRENNAN was born in 1870. He gained a reputation as a 'character' around Sydney.
American author STEPHEN CRANE was born in 1871. He wrote "The Red Badge Of Courage", a remarkably realistic account of the American Civil War.
English painter L.S. LOWRY was born in 1887.

Australian humanist philosopher Professor JOHN ANDERSON, who taught his students to question censorship, was born in 1893. He once lent the banned book "Ulysses" to his pupils, disguising it as a "Book Of Common Prayer".
Australian VFL footballer EDWARD "CARJI" GREEVES was born in 1903. He played for Geelong, and won the first BROWNLOW medal, wearing guernsey number 20.
South African golfer GARY PLAYER, who won all four of the world's major golfing championships, was born in 1935.
Australian actor and theatre director JOHN BELL was born in 1940.
American guitarist, singer and songwriter with the group 'America', DAN PEEK, was born in 1950.
British drummer with the band 'Def Leppard', RICK ALLEN, was born in 1963.
** EVENTS **
1755 : Two-thirds of the Portugese city of Lisbon was
devastated by severe earthquakes, leaving a death toll estimated at up to 60-thousand.
1793 : British anti-Catholic LORD GEORGE GORDON died in
Newgate Prison, convicted of libelling MARIE ANTOINETTE (he stirred up the so called GORDON riots in 1790).
1814 : The European Congress opened in Vienna, following
NAPOLEON's defeat.
1858 : The East India Company's long reign over India

came to an end, when the administration of the country was passed to Britain's QUEEN VICTORIA. The East India Company, formed in 1600, had acted as an agent of British imperialism since the early 18th century.
1880 : A trapeze was attached to a balloon and sent into

the air above the gates of Paris, on which professional gymnast AUGUST NAVARRE was to perform several tricks. He had been advised to fasten himself to the trapeze, but didn't, and fell from a height of about two thousand feet. His body left a hole about two feet deep in a nearby garden bed.
1895 : The first motoring organisation, the American
Motor League, was founded.
1914 : At the Battle of Coronel off Chile, the British
ships Good Hope and Monmouth were sunk by German cruisers with the loss of 1,600 lives.
1922 : The first radio licences went on sale in Britain,
costing ten shillings.
1946 : The premiere of "A Matter Of Life And Death" with
DAVID NIVEN was held at the Empire, Leicester Square - Britain's first Royal Command performance.
1950 : Two Puerto Rican nationalists (OSCAR COLLAZO and

GIRSEL TORRESOLA) made an attempt on the life of United States President HARRY S.TRUMAN in Washington D.C. TRUMAN was in his private residence across the street from the White House, when the pair tried to shoot their way in. Twenty-seven shots were fired as TRUMAN's guards exchanged gunfire with the would-be assassins. The president was unharmed, but one guard and both gunmen were killed. TRUMAN later commented that "a president should expect these things".
1954 : Algerian nationalists began a war of independence
against the French.
1961 : The body of JOSEPH STALIN (JOSEPH VISSARIONOVICH

DJUGASHVILI) was removed from the mausoleum in Moscow's Red Square, where it had laid next to LENIN's since his death in 1953. Following a campaign of "de-Stalinisation", the city of Stalingrad was later renamed Volgagrad, and all public memorials to STALIN were removed in East Germany.
1967 : "Rolling Stone" magazine made its debut as the
first national rock 'n' roll periodical in the United States.
1968 : United States President LYNDON JOHNSON ordered a

total and unconditional end to the bombing of North Vietnam, in a bid to breathe life into stalled peace talks in Paris. In return, the North Vietnamese agreed to allow the South Vietnamese to take part in the Paris talks.
1969 : Victoria police revealed that Britain's Great

Train Robber RONALD BIGGS had slipped out of their grasp when he was startled by fire sirens. BIGGS had been hiding out in the Dandenong Ranges outside Melbourne with his wife and family since escaping from a Brtiish jail in 1964. Police had planned to capture BIGGS in a rented cottage, but he fled just a few hours before the proposed raid when he became alarmed at the sound of fire sirens.
1972 : American poet EZRA POUND died in Venice at the
age of 87.
1973 : The last issue of the underground magazine "OZ"
was published in Britain.
1974 : Great Train Robber RONALD BIGGS (see above)
revealed in a television interview in Rio De Janiero that he was homesick for Australia.
1977 : 'Gold and Black' gave trainer BART CUMMINGS a
record 6th win in the Melbourne Cup.
1977 : Sheffield Shield cricket newcomer Tasmania lost
its first match, to Western Australia by an innings and 14 runs.
1983 : New Zealand stayer 'Kiwi' came from last place to
win the Melbourne Cup.
1984 : RAJIV GANDHI was sworn in as India's Premier.
1985 : American comedian PHIL SILVERS died at the age of
73. He was known for his role as 'Sergeant Bilko' in the tv series, "You'll Never Get Rich", which was later retitled "The PHIL SILVERS Show".
1985 : Genetic fingerprinting was used for the first time
in Britain to prove paternity.
1986 : The national party government of Premier SIR JOH
BJELKE-PETERSON was returned to power in Queensland.
1988 : 'Empire Rose' won the Melbourne Cup, creating a
new weight-carrying record for a mare.
1988 : Twenty year old ANTHONY FARRELL was charged with
murdering two police officers in the so-called 'Walsh Street' killings in Melbourne.
1988 : The faithful sidekick of 'Batman', 'Robin' was
killed off in edition number 428 of DC Comics. 'Robin' was dynamited to death by 'The Joker', following a readers' poll showing the character was no longer popular.
1989 : Pakistan Prime Minister BENAZIR BHUTTO narrowly
survived a no-confidence motion.
1993 : The Maastricht Treaty came into effect, creating a
new "European Union".
1995 : Balkan leaders met with chief U.S. mediator
Richard Holbrooke at Dayton, Ohio, at the start of talks to end four years of war.
1995 : South Africans voted in their first all-race
local government elections, completing the destruction of the apartheid system.
